title: Oman announces ceasefire between the United States and the Houthis
body:
On 6 May 2025 Oman, acting as mediator, announced a ceasefire between the United States and Yemen's Houthis. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi posted the statement online, saying the deal followed recent discussions and contacts aimed at de-escalation. Under the terms, neither side would target the other, including American vessels, with the aim of protecting freedom of navigation and commercial shipping in the Red Sea.

President Donald Trump said the United States would end its strikes after the Houthis agreed to stop attacking ships, and that the Houthis had "capitulated." He did not directly mention Houthi attacks on Israel. Arab News reported that the Houthis gave no official response at the time of reporting, and that their political bureau had earlier said Israeli strikes would not pass without a response.

US bombing had run near-daily for seven weeks, and the Pentagon said US strikes had hit more than 1,000 targets in Yemen since mid-March. An Agence France-Presse tally of Houthi figures put the death toll from the US campaign at 300. Separately, the Houthi news agency Saba, citing the health ministry, reported one person killed at Sanaa airport and two at a power station in Israeli strikes that day, with 35 wounded. The truce covered only US-Houthi relations and left open the Houthi campaign against Israel.
